chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abdullah ibn Maymoun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Yaqoub (peace be upon him) said to his son: 'O my son, do not commit adultery, for if the bird commits adultery, its feathers fall off.'
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical explanation for adultery given by Prophet Yaqoub in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) conveys a metaphorical warning from Prophet Yaqoub (Jacob) to his son, likening the spiritual and physical degradation of adultery to a bird losing its feathers. This imagery underscores the concept of *fasad* (corruption) and the loss of one's natural integrity and dignity, a theme frequently explored in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the consequences of major sins.
